_doc: Three-stream timeline of workflow evolution. The analyzer joins session.startTime against shippedAt/adoptedAt to compute per-session era tags emitted in metrics-by-era.json. Three streams keep agent-side rule edits (machine-extractable from git), user-side practice adoptions (manually authored at session wrap via Handoff Architect Phase 4 field #9), and infrastructure/tooling changes attributable independently. Retroactive seed dates are best-effort: agentRuleEdits derive precise timestamps from git log .github/instructions/; userPracticeAdoptions and infraToolingChanges use the earliest evidence date found in handoffs/ADRs/user-memory. Adoption-date precision claims no better than +/- 1 week for inferred entries. See ADR-0036.

agentRuleEdits.name: Pre-restructure baseline (monolith)
agentRuleEdits.description: Era-tagging anchor: prior to commit 48309ab the agent rules lived in .github/copilot-instructions.md as a single file. Sessions before 2026-05-28 fall in this era.

agentRuleEdits.name: Restructure into scoped skill files
agentRuleEdits.description: Split monolith into per-scope instruction files (compliance / logic / persistence / security / structural / ui). Established the file-per-concern shape every later rule edit assumes.

agentRuleEdits.name: Sharded docs/memory/ MCP graph backup
agentRuleEdits.description: Added shard-file backup layer under docs/memory/ so MCP graph corruption is recoverable from git history rather than a single JSONL file.

agentRuleEdits.name: Mandatory Post-Edit Scan gate
agentRuleEdits.description: After any file edit the agent must call get_errors on every modified file and fix any errors before handing back. Silently skipping the scan is a compliance failure.

agentRuleEdits.name: Workflow Logger skill + Phase 0 recipe lookup
agentRuleEdits.description: Added Workflow Logger to Phase 4 + an advisory Phase 0 step to check docs/workflows/ for a matching recipe before starting a task.
agentRuleEdits.source: persistence.instructions.md Workflow Logger, compliance.instructions.md Phase 0 step 0

agentRuleEdits.name: Confidence Trap + Symbol Check Gate + Memory Keeper hard gate
agentRuleEdits.description: Three rules: high confidence does not exempt the lookup stack; Symbol Check Gate forbids grep for symbol names; Memory Keeper must verify entity presence via open_nodes before any add_observations call.

agentRuleEdits.name: TDD as first-class Phase 2.5 skill
agentRuleEdits.description: Added Phase 2.5 RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for src/lib, src/app/api, src/data with mandatory verify steps. ADR-0018 captures the decision.

agentRuleEdits.name: Harden MCP memory infra + session continuity
agentRuleEdits.description: Locked the read-then-write Memory Keeper protocol with explicit open_nodes pre-check, shard-backup pairing, and session-continuity discipline at session start.

agentRuleEdits.name: Grep Gate (mandatory self-justification)
agentRuleEdits.description: Every grep_search invocation must include a one-line justification: Grep target is X, not a code symbol because Y. Phase 1 of the workflow self-improvement loop.

agentRuleEdits.name: Terminal-Echo Rule
agentRuleEdits.description: Terminal output echoed back as a user message must not trigger a new assistant turn unless exit code is non-zero or input is needed. Phase 1 of the workflow self-improvement loop.

agentRuleEdits.name: Phase 4 Composite Gate for handoff
agentRuleEdits.description: Handoff doc may only be written after Memory Keeper has run in the same response. Phase 1 of the workflow self-improvement loop.
agentRuleEdits.source: persistence.instructions.md Handoff Architect Phase 4 Composite Gate

agentRuleEdits.name: Workflow Cadence Check (Phase 0 prelude)
agentRuleEdits.description: Every new session reads docs/chat-exports/analysis/workflow-reviews.json and surfaces days-since-last-review with on-cadence / due / overdue thresholds. Phase 1 of the workflow self-improvement loop.

agentRuleEdits.name: Handoff Architect Phase 4 field 8 (Workflow Review Cadence)
agentRuleEdits.description: Handoff doc must report days-since-last-review and append to workflow-reviews.json when this session performed a review. Phase 1 of the workflow self-improvement loop.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Session-start handoff read
userPracticeAdoptions.description: User adopted the practice of opening each session with a Session Start marker plus a summary of the most recent handoff. Codified shortly after into Handoff Architect CRITICAL clause.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Codegraph-first lookup discipline
userPracticeAdoptions.description: User explicitly flagged grep-for-symbol abuse as a recurring miss; established the codegraph_context / codegraph_search precedence over grep_search for symbol queries.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: E.T.C. (Execute -> Test -> Commit) ship rhythm
userPracticeAdoptions.description: Per-change atomic ETC cycle. ADHD-friendly: clear stages, completion signal after each, atomic commits stay revertible, test gate catches breakage before commit. Used as default ship rhythm on focused changes.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Verification-first bias
userPracticeAdoptions.description: When choosing between memory writes / docs / config tidying and end-to-end verification, default to verification. Lab evidence (real request, real DB, real UI) catches integration drift unit tests cannot.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Voice dictation for prompt authoring
userPracticeAdoptions.description: User started authoring prompts via voice dictation. Affects user-message length, syntax patterns, and the surface text the analyzer scans for negation regex.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Weekly workflow-review cadence
userPracticeAdoptions.description: User adopted a weekly cadence of analyzing chat exports, distilling friction patterns, and shipping rule edits before resuming feature work. Baseline 21-session review performed 2026-06-19.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Standalone-product framing for in-repo experiments
userPracticeAdoptions.description: When a system grows beyond a feature into something that could plausibly serve other tenants (Shipyard is the first instance), explicitly treat the current repo as the incubator/first tenant rather than the permanent home. Surfaced as Extractability NFR in ADR-0038 §5: generic schema field names, configurable paths in scripts, no host-repo-specific assumptions baked into the artifact. Practice question to ask at any cross-cutting design decision: 'would this work as a tenant of itself?' If yes, write it that way from day one — extraction stays cheap. If no, defend why the coupling is permanent. Replaces the implicit 'features live where they're born' default that made the parked Shipyard plan vulnerable to lock-in.
userPracticeAdoptions.replacedPractice: implicit 'features live where they're born' default

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Three-layer automation model (Bookkeeping / Pattern-detection / Semantic-content)
userPracticeAdoptions.description: Mental framework for deciding what to automate in any knowledge-management or context-engineering system. Layer 1 (Bookkeeping: dates, fingerprints, scaffolding, file metadata) — automate aggressively; cheap to compute, deterministic, no judgment required. Layer 2 (Pattern detection: recurring recipes, friction signals) — mine-and-propose; machine surfaces candidates, human promotes. Layer 3 (Semantic content: design intent, knownTraps, the "why this is accepted, not a regression" notes) — must stay curated; codebase cannot observe its own intent, closure-capture bugs cannot be derived from line counts. Surfaced from user critique that the new-slice authoring workflow looked like a 7-step manual process. The model is the directional answer: not all of it can or should be automated — but the distinction is now explicit, and every Shipyard tool ships with a Layer-1/2/3 declaration of what it touches. Replaces the implicit 'automate it all' / 'curate it all' false binary.
userPracticeAdoptions.evidenceSource: This session (commit 759e389 — slice scaffold script auto-fills Layer 1 only; ADR-0038); docs/c-yard/effectiveness-review.md (hypotheses 3 + 4 frozen as testable claims).
userPracticeAdoptions.replacedPractice: implicit 'automate it all' / 'curate it all' false binary

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Live-smoke-before-commit verification pattern
userPracticeAdoptions.description: When committing a refactor that crosses a real boundary (external API, third-party service, network protocol), augment hermetic mocked tests with an env-gated live smoke suite that exercises the actual provider. Acceptance is loose — happy-path success OR known acceptable error codes (503/429) both count as green — so the suite stays useful even when quota is exhausted. Pattern proven on ADR-0044 Day 5: live smoke against Gemini caught decommissioned gemini-1.5 fallback models (returned 404 NOT_FOUND) that no hermetic mock would have surfaced, AND let the chain be remediated in the same sprint window before the ADR was promoted to Accepted. Default for any future PR that touches an external integration boundary.
userPracticeAdoptions.evidenceSource: src/lib/ai/smoke.live.test.ts + scripts/smoke-ai-live.ps1; commit 1472f75; ADR-0044 Acceptance subsection (commit 18c0fbb)
userPracticeAdoptions.replacedPractice: hermetic-only test coverage on external-API boundaries

infraToolingChanges.name: Cline + Ollama gemma4:26b + codegraph MCP local LLM stack
infraToolingChanges.description: Validated 3-tier cost-control routing: Cline + gemma4 for routine codegraph / memory / single-file edits; Copilot picker (Gemini Flash) for cheap cloud; Copilot Opus for premium. Reduces premium-request burn.

infraToolingChanges.description: PowerShell script that POSTs a spec to Ollama, extracts fenced code blocks, writes files, runs a test command, and feeds back failures for up to N repair attempts. Replaces Copilot turns for well-spec'd pure utilities and TDD GREEN steps.

infraToolingChanges.name: scripts/analyze-chat-exports.mjs
infraToolingChanges.description: Read-only analyzer over docs/chat-exports/raw/*.jsonl. Emits 5-category metrics dashboard plus worst-3 friction digests plus optional deep-dive. Foundation for Phase 1 + Phase 2 of the workflow self-improvement loop.

infraToolingChanges.name: ADR-0037 Proposed — Shipyard context-engineering layer (Slice foundational primitive)
infraToolingChanges.description: Proposed ADR committing to Shipyard as umbrella context-engineering layer with Slice as Phase 1 foundational primitive (topic-keyed JSON manifests unifying WHY+HOW+VALIDATION+PROVENANCE). Memory graph becomes legacy read-fallback during transition. Six-pillar vision committed in principle; Phase 2-6 deferred to per-phase ADRs (0038+).

infraToolingChanges.name: Shipyard 6-phase roadmap (Proposed)
infraToolingChanges.description: Seasonal sprint plan for ADR-0037: Phase 0 (foundations, shipped) → Phase 1 (Slice unification, next) → Phase 2 (cached tool outputs) → Phase 3 (frequency priming) → Phase 4 (file-watcher push invalidation) → Phase 5 (background diff worker) → Phase 6 (per-Slice observability). Each future phase backed by its own ADR (0038-0043).

infraToolingChanges.name: ADR-0038 Proposed — Slice schema lock + Shipyard Extractability NFR
infraToolingChanges.description: Phase 1 sprint-kickoff ADR. Locks the three open Slice schema decisions from ADR-0037: D1=B (cross-slice relations in docs/c-yard/_index.json adjacency list); D2=B (cross-cutting knowledge stays in user-memory with version-bound vs codebase-bound boundary rule); D3=B (Shipyard repo-only, no scope tiers). Adds D4=B (long-term home is a standalone shipyard/ repo; Resumsify is Phase 1 incubator) and Extractability NFR §5 (no Resumsify-specific names/paths/assumptions in Phase 1 artifacts). G1=A (one slice per UI surface, split at >~15 files). Provisional Phase 1 defaults: fingerprint staleness = warn-and-serve with staleSurfaces[]; evidence schema = { sessions: [{ id, turnExcerpt, toolCallIndex }] }. Phase 1 commit 1 cleared to ship. Same commit also amends ADR-0037 with Decision #7 (long-term home) and Con #6 (extractability tax).

infraToolingChanges.name: Shipyard Phase 1 — Slice unification rollup (5 commits)
infraToolingChanges.description: Phase 1 shipped end-to-end: (1) first slice docs/c-yard/worklog-editor.json + README schema spec [1ff1454]; (2) analyzer --mine-traversals flag for Layer 2 pattern detection [15844f9]; (3) Phase 0 lookup-stack rewrite to consult slice FIRST with mandatory escape-valve audit trail [53204d6]; (4) slice refresh from dry-run evidence — split monolithic knownTrap into 3 sub-bugs, added refreshHistory[] [3362516]; (5) scripts/slice-scaffold.mjs to auto-fill Layer 1 bookkeeping for new slices, cutting cold-start cost from ~45 min to ~3 min curated review [759e389]. Effectiveness hypotheses + review cadence captured at docs/c-yard/effectiveness-review.md.

infraToolingChanges.name: ADR-0044 Proposed — AI provider router (Scope B), 3-layer architecture
infraToolingChanges.description: Week-long sprint kickoff. Scope B locked: consolidate lib/ai.ts + lib/gemini.ts into one façade with task-class routing (5 classes: chat/extract/ground/reason/summarize), add gemini-2.5-pro as premium tier reusing existing GEMINI_API_KEY, stub cost-guard hooks (userId + onUsage emitted but not enforced until multi-tenancy lands). Plug-in provider surface keeps Anthropic/OpenAI/local-models open as future additions. Three-layer architecture committed: L1 Provider Router (this week), L2 Skill Registry (future ADR), L3 MCP Tool Surface (future ADR). Scope C (FirebaseAIProvider/AICoreProvider/BYOK family) documented as Forward Path §1 honoring ADR-0021's Play Store push deferral. No slice manifest written: AI provider is backend infra not UI surface per ADR-0038 §G1; knowledge instead lives in extended AIServicesLayer memory entity. Originally planned as ADR-0022 in conversation; slot taken by worklog Grill Me markdown round-trip; bumped to 0044 to avoid Shipyard's 0039-0043 reservations.
